lede: October US consumer prices rose faster than expected, pushing a December Fed hike to fully priced and sending the 2-year yield up the most in a single day since April 2025. Gold lost about 2.6% and US stocks slipped, while Asian equities firmed this morning and gold is stabilising near $4,040.
snapshot_time: Gold ≈03:25 TRT · Brent ≈03:50 TRT · FX & US500 = Tue close

focus.text: Dropped about 2.6% Tuesday as hotter CPI lifted yields and the dollar; steadying near $4,039 on the 4,025–4,036 support band. Today: ECB speakers; US bond market shut for Veterans Day.
Fell about 0.5% to 1.1163 as US rate-hike bets firmed; now below the 1.1187 midpoint of its 1.1089–1.1271 range. Main risk today: Lagarde and other ECB remarks.

technicals.indicators: H1 RSI(14) dropped from 64 to 28 (oversold) before a slight uptick · price below all key moving averages
technicals.note: The CPI selloff wiped out Monday's rally and left gold sitting on its first support band after rejecting the 4,145–4,157 area.

technicals.indicators: RSI near 50 · MACD histogram flat around zero · long-term bearish trendline overhead
technicals.note: Price is drifting to the lower half of a multi-week range under a downward-sloping trendline; 1.1089 marks lows last seen in May 2025.

technicals.indicators: Trading around the 200-day MA ≈ 73,100 · options skew still favours puts
technicals.note: A double top at 81,890/81,080 broke its 75,628 neckline on 5 Nov; bitcoin is now testing the 200-day average after the CPI-driven dip.

calendar.event: ECB's Lagarde, Cipollone, Kazaks and Nagel speak
Veterans Day: US bond market closed, stocks open

news.text: US CPI rose 0.4% m/m in October and core 0.3%, each a tenth above forecasts; no annual rate was published because of the shutdown data gap.
A December hike is now fully priced; Governor Waller floated 50bp if inflation stays hot and Dallas Fed's Logan called for at least 50bp more.
The 2-year Treasury yield jumped about 17bp to 4.73%, its biggest daily rise since April 2025; the 10-year ended near 4.98%.
S&P 500 fell 0.38% to 7,520.93 and the Nasdaq 0.74%, with Nvidia down again amid a board probe into its CEO; Kospi and Nikkei rose this morning.
Brent touched a two-month low near $89.2 on hopes the Iran conflict could end soon, then recovered toward $92.5 in Asian trade.
Euro also weighed by uncertainty over Lagarde's early exit; Klaas Knot and Pablo Hernández de Cos are seen as front-runners, with euro finance ministers reviewing candidates this week.
Hot US inflation knocked bitcoin to around $72,640 on Tuesday, briefly below its 200-day average; fear & greed gauge slipped to 29.
US spot bitcoin ETFs saw a third straight outflow day (–$201M on 9 Nov), taking November to about –$1.48B; ether funds lost $185M.
MSCI announces its index review tonight; Strategy and Metaplanet are seen as possible removals, effective after the 30 Nov close.
Initia's layer-1 network was halted after an attack, according to exchange market reports.
Zcash jumped over 10% and Internet Computer about 8% ahead of DFINITY's planned Cloud Engines launch this week.
Miami-Dade County began accepting bitcoin for property-tax payments.
